description: 1-(1-Naphthylmethyl)quinolinium chloride (CAS 65322-65-8 ) is a quaternary ammonium salt used as a specialty reagent in pharmaceutical and biotechnology research. It functions as a charged heterocyclic building block and ionic species capable of pH-modulating activity in controlled research environments. In pharmaceutical research, it serves as a reference compound or synthetic intermediate in the development of quinolinium-based active pharmaceutical ingredients. Biotechnology laboratories use it in assay development and biochemical screening where structurally defined quaternary nitrogen compounds are required. Its well-defined ionic character makes it applicable in buffer system studies where cationic species influence solution pH behavior at the research scale. It also appears in the synthesis of novel heterocyclic libraries targeting receptor binding studies. 1-(1-Naphthylmethyl)quinolinium chloride is supplied as a solid powder, typically in high-purity research grades suited to laboratory and pharmaceutical development use. Standard offerings are positioned at ≥97% or ≥98% purity, consistent with pharmaceutical reference and synthetic intermediate applications. Packaging is generally available in small quantities ranging from milligram to multi-gram scale, reflecting its primary use in R&D rather than bulk industrial production. This chemical is handled according to standard laboratory safety protocols for quaternary ammonium compounds. The compound is valued for its stability and predictable behavior in organic synthesis and analytical chemistry. Researchers utilize its unique naphthylmethyl substitution to explore specific molecular interactions within complex biological or chemical systems.
